plugin.gcm.title: GCM (Galois/Counter Mode)
plugin.gcm.preset.mcgrew-viega-tc2: McGrew–Viega test case 2 (one zero block, AES-128)
plugin.gcm.preset.mcgrew-viega-tc4: McGrew–Viega test case 4 (with additional authenticated data)
plugin.gcm.preset.mcgrew-viega-tc6: McGrew–Viega test case 6 (60-byte IV: J0 via GHASH)
plugin.gcm.preset.gmac: GMAC: authenticate the AAD only, no plaintext (test case 4 key)
plugin.gcm.preset.decrypt-valid: Decrypt test case 4 with its valid tag
plugin.gcm.preset.decrypt-forged: Decrypt test case 4 with one tag bit flipped (FAIL)
plugin.gcm.param.cipherHint: A block cipher with 128-bit blocks, such as AES. GCM needs 16-byte blocks for GHASH.
plugin.gcm.param.keyHint: A key the block cipher accepts, e.g. 16, 24 or 32 bytes for AES.
plugin.gcm.param.ivHint: 1 to 64 bytes. 12 bytes (96 bits) is the fast path; any other length goes through GHASH to form J0. Never reuse an IV with the same key.
plugin.gcm.param.aadHint: 0 to 64 bytes. The AAD is authenticated but not encrypted, e.g. a packet header. It may be empty.
plugin.gcm.param.inputHint: 0 to 64 bytes: the plaintext when encrypting, the ciphertext when decrypting. Empty input turns GCM into GMAC.
plugin.gcm.param.tagHint: Only for decryption: the authentication tag that came with the ciphertext, exactly as long as the tag length.
plugin.gcm.param.tagBytesHint: SP 800-38D allows 16, 15, 14, 13 and 12 bytes; 8 and 4 bytes only within the limits of its Appendix C.
plugin.gcm.param.tagBytesOption.8: 8 bytes (64 bits, Appendix C limits only)
plugin.gcm.param.tagBytesOption.4: 4 bytes (32 bits, Appendix C limits only)
plugin.gcm.region.candidate: Candidate plaintext (held back until the tag is checked)
plugin.gcm.op.hashKey: Derive the hash subkey H = E_K(0¹²⁸)
plugin.gcm.op.encryptCounter: Encrypt the counter block with E_K
plugin.gcm.op.xorKeystream: XOR the input with the keystream
plugin.gcm.op.ghashBlock: GHASH: XOR a block in and multiply by H
plugin.gcm.op.tag: Form the tag T = MSB_t(S ⊕ E_K(J0))
plugin.gcm.formula.encrypt: C = GCTR_K(inc32(J0), P), T = MSB_t(GCTR_K(J0, GHASH_H(A ‖ C ‖ lengths)))
plugin.gcm.formula.decrypt: T′ = MSB_t(GCTR_K(J0, GHASH_H(A ‖ C ‖ lengths))); P = GCTR_K(inc32(J0), C) only if T′ = T
plugin.gcm.field.initial: Y₀ = 0. GHASH starts once the setup has derived H: Yᵢ = (Yᵢ₋₁ ⊕ Bᵢ) • H in GF(2¹²⁸)
plugin.gcm.step.initial: GCM encrypts the {{bytes}}-byte plaintext P with {{cipher}} in counter mode and authenticates it, together with the {{aadBytes}}-byte additional authenticated data (AAD), by a {{tagBits}}-bit tag. First it derives two values from the key and the {{ivBytes}}-byte IV: the hash subkey H and the pre-counter block J0.
plugin.gcm.step.initialGmac: The input is empty, so this is GMAC: GCM encrypts nothing and only authenticates the {{aadBytes}}-byte AAD by a {{tagBits}}-bit tag. It still derives the hash subkey H and the pre-counter block J0 from the key ({{cipher}}) and the {{ivBytes}}-byte IV.
plugin.gcm.step.initialDecrypt: GCM decryption with {{cipher}}: it recomputes the {{tagBits}}-bit tag over the {{aadBytes}}-byte AAD and the {{bytes}}-byte ciphertext C, using the {{ivBytes}}-byte IV, and compares it with the received tag {{tag}}. Only if both tags are equal does it release the plaintext.
plugin.gcm.step.hashKey: {{cipher}} encrypts the all-zero block: H = E_K(0¹²⁸) = {{h}}. H is the hash subkey: GHASH multiplies by it in GF(2¹²⁸).
plugin.gcm.step.j0Fast: The IV {{iv}} has 96 bits, the fast path: J0 = IV ‖ 0³¹ ‖ 1 = {{j0}}.
plugin.gcm.step.j0Ghash: The IV has {{ivBits}} bits, not 96, so J0 = GHASH_H(IV ‖ 0^(s+64) ‖ [len(IV)]₆₄). IV block {{n}} of {{count}}: Y{{n}} = (Y{{prev}} ⊕ B{{n}}) • H = ({{before}} ⊕ {{block}}) • H = {{product}}.
plugin.gcm.step.j0GhashLength: Block {{n}} of {{count}} is the IV length in bits, [len(IV)]₆₄ = {{block}} for the {{ivBits}}-bit IV. Y{{n}} = (Y{{prev}} ⊕ B{{n}}) • H = ({{before}} ⊕ {{block}}) • H = {{product}}. That is J0.
plugin.gcm.step.inc32First: CB1 = inc32(J0) = {{counter}}. The first counter block is one above J0; J0 itself is kept for the tag.
plugin.gcm.step.inc32: CB{{n}} = inc32(CB{{prev}}) = {{counter}}. Only the last 32 bits count up (mod 2³²); the first 96 bits never change.
plugin.gcm.step.encryptCounter: Block {{n}}: {{cipher}} encrypts CB{{n}} = {{counter}} to the keystream block {{keystream}}.
plugin.gcm.step.xorKeystreamPartial: Block {{n}}: only {{used}} input bytes are left, so only the first {{used}} keystream bytes are used: {{input}} ⊕ {{keystream}} = {{output}}. The other {{unused}} keystream bytes are thrown away; no padding is needed.
plugin.gcm.step.xorKeystreamWithheld: Block {{n}}: {{input}} ⊕ {{keystream}} gives a candidate plaintext block. GCM holds it back until the tag is checked, so it is not shown yet.
plugin.gcm.step.xorKeystreamWithheldPart: Block {{n}}: only {{used}} input bytes are left, so only the first {{used}} keystream bytes are used: {{input}} ⊕ {{keystream}} gives a candidate plaintext block, held back until the tag is checked. The other {{unused}} keystream bytes are thrown away; no padding is needed.
plugin.gcm.step.ghashAad: GHASH, AAD block {{index}}: Y{{n}} = (Y{{prev}} ⊕ A{{index}}) • H = ({{before}} ⊕ {{block}}) • H = {{product}}.
plugin.gcm.step.ghashAadPartial: GHASH, AAD block {{index}}: only {{used}} AAD bytes are left, so {{zeros}} zero bytes fill the block. Y{{n}} = (Y{{prev}} ⊕ A{{index}}) • H = ({{before}} ⊕ {{block}}) • H = {{product}}.
plugin.gcm.step.ghashCiphertext: GHASH, ciphertext block {{index}}: Y{{n}} = (Y{{prev}} ⊕ C{{index}}) • H = ({{before}} ⊕ {{block}}) • H = {{product}}. GCM authenticates the ciphertext, not the plaintext.
plugin.gcm.step.ghashCiphertextPartial: GHASH, ciphertext block {{index}}: only {{used}} ciphertext bytes are left, so {{zeros}} zero bytes fill the block. Y{{n}} = (Y{{prev}} ⊕ C{{index}}) • H = ({{before}} ⊕ {{block}}) • H = {{product}}.
plugin.gcm.step.lengthBlock: The length block [len(A)]₆₄ ‖ [len(C)]₆₄ = {{block}} holds {{aadBits}} AAD bits and {{ciphertextBits}} ciphertext bits, so zero padding cannot hide a change of length. Y{{n}} = (Y{{prev}} ⊕ lengths) • H = ({{before}} ⊕ {{block}}) • H = {{product}}. This is S, the GHASH of everything GCM authenticates.
plugin.gcm.step.encryptJ0: {{cipher}} encrypts J0 = {{j0}}: E_K(J0) = {{mask}}. This block masks S; without the key nobody can compute it.
plugin.gcm.step.tag: T = S ⊕ E_K(J0) = {{s}} ⊕ {{mask}} = {{tag}}. The tag travels with the ciphertext.
plugin.gcm.step.tagTruncated: S ⊕ E_K(J0) = {{s}} ⊕ {{mask}} = {{full}}. The tag keeps only the first {{tagBytes}} bytes: T = MSB_{{tagBits}}(…) = {{tag}}. A forger guesses a valid {{tagBits}}-bit tag with probability of about 2^−{{tagBits}} per attempt.
plugin.gcm.step.tagRecomputed: T′ = S ⊕ E_K(J0) = {{s}} ⊕ {{mask}} = {{tag}}. This is the tag the received data should carry.
plugin.gcm.step.tagRecomputedTruncated: S ⊕ E_K(J0) = {{s}} ⊕ {{mask}} = {{full}}. Keep the first {{tagBytes}} bytes: T′ = MSB_{{tagBits}}(…) = {{tag}}. This is the tag the received data should carry.
plugin.gcm.step.verifyOk: T′ = {{computed}} equals the received tag T = {{received}}: the data is authentic, so GCM releases the held-back plaintext.
plugin.gcm.step.verifyFail: FAIL: T′ = {{computed}} differs from the received tag T = {{received}}. The IV, the AAD, the ciphertext or the tag was changed, or the key is wrong. GCM returns only FAIL and releases no plaintext: the held-back candidate from the CTR phase is wiped.
plugin.gcm.error.invalidParams: Give the key, the IV, the AAD, the input and the tag as hex text.
plugin.gcm.error.keyLength: The key has {{length}} bytes; it needs 1 to 64.
plugin.gcm.error.ivLength: The IV has {{length}} bytes; it needs 1 to 64.
plugin.gcm.error.aadLength: The AAD has {{length}} bytes; it may have at most 64.
plugin.gcm.error.inputLength: The input has {{length}} bytes; it may have at most 64.
plugin.gcm.error.tagBytes: Choose a tag length of 16, 15, 14, 13, 12, 8 or 4 bytes.
plugin.gcm.error.tagLength: The tag has {{length}} bytes; with this tag length it needs exactly {{tagBytes}}.
plugin.gcm.error.blockSize: GCM needs a block cipher with 16-byte blocks; this one has {{blockSize}}-byte blocks.
